A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InstructRAG despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-benchmark evaluations, ablations, sensitivity and transfer experiments, and case studies in Section 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds RetRobust comparisons, HumanEval transfer results, and GPT-4o-based evaluation.

M1.justification: Both versions synthesize denoising rationales and use them for in-context learning or supervised fine-tuning with the same objective. v2's Algorithm 1 summarizes the existing procedure; applying the trained model to code generation does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates five QA benchmarks and transfer among QA tasks. v2 retains that coverage and adds HumanEval code generation using a PopQA-trained InstructRAG-FT model, extending evaluation to a substantially different task and output domain (Section 3.4, Table 5a).

E2.justification: v2 adds one comparator family, RetRobust, to the retained main comparison suite. Table 3 reports its Llama-2-13B results on Natural Questions and 2WikiMultiHopQA and its Llama-3-Instruct-8B results across all five QA benchmarks; these comparisons are absent from v1 Table 5.

E3.justification: v2 adds distinct evaluation protocols: QA-to-code transfer with and without retrieval using pass@1 and pass@10, and GPT-4o semantic judging on Natural Questions alongside pattern matching. It also specifies training settings for the added RetRobust baseline. The original QA splits, retrievers, and existing methods' training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens the analyses with transfer beyond QA and a check of whether comparative findings survive semantic rather than lexical evaluation (Table 5). The original ablations, demonstration sensitivity, retrieval-noise tests, and QA-transfer analyses remain; the case studies move from Section 3.5 to Appendix B.

E5.justification: The shaded bands in Figure 3a are retained without new descriptions of their statistical meaning. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures; its added tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Original main-table and ablation values are unchanged, but v2 adds substantive results for RetRobust, HumanEval, and semantic judging. For example, HumanEval retrieval pass@1 is 64.6 for InstructRAG-FT versus 59.8 for the base model; GPT-4o-judged Natural Questions scores are 69.7 for InstructRAG-FT versus 65.1 for vanilla SFT. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and likelihood objective in Equation 1 remain equivalent. Algorithm 1 and explicit retriever notation restate the existing procedure; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2 adds none.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: self-synthesized denoising without additional supervision, applicability to ICL and fine-tuning, robust generalization, and the reported 8.3% average improvement across five benchmarks. The new experiments support these retained claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 attributes RetRobust's multi-hop performance to GPT-3-generated intermediate supervision and associates code-transfer gains with more explanatory code comments. It also interprets the semantic-judging results and removes v1's reassurance that evaluation biases do not greatly affect its method. Existing denoising and QA-transfer explanations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds RetRobust implementation details: a learning rate of 2e-5, two training epochs generally, and five epochs on the authors' augmented 2WikiMultiHopQA data. Existing InstructRAG hardware, hyperparameters, retrieval configuration, and code-access information remain unchanged. Consolidated prompt tables largely repeat previously disclosed instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused discussion and citations covering RetRobust, code-generation evaluation, LLM judging, prompt compression, and earlier rationalization research. It explicitly contrasts its supervision requirements with RetRobust as well as Self-RAG. The central positioning around self-generated explicit denoising remains intact.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'with Explicit Denoising' to 'via Self-Synthesized Rationales.' v2 adds a pseudocode overview, edits baseline and analysis prose, standardizes the few-shot baseline terminology, and relocates case studies to Appendix B and prompts to Appendix C. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1 and the two-panel analysis Table 5, expands the main results table with RetRobust rows, and moves Figures 5–6 to the appendix. The separate main-text inference prompts are consolidated with appendix templates. Existing figures retain their content and visual design, making this a localized display reorganization.

improvement.justification: RetRobust strengthens the comparison with another noise-robust method, while HumanEval transfer and GPT-4o judging partly address v1's acknowledged limitations concerning QA-only evidence and lexical evaluation. These additions improve empirical support without removing existing evidence. The gain is limited by testing only one non-QA benchmark and by missing judge prompts and code-generation sampling details, which constrain reproducibility and interpretation.
